content:
Hello!
I'm a master's student in Security and Applied Logic from Bucharest, Romania. As my first major project in Lean 4, I have formalized Okasaki-style Red-Black Trees.

I've implemented the core data structure and fully proven that the insert function preserves all structural invariants (the BST property, uniform black height, and valid red-black coloring). To keep the dependency graph lightweight, I built this using Lean's native Ord class instead of Mathlib's equivalents, passing transitivity and symmetry as explicit hypotheses to the main theorem.

I noticed that verified data structures (like RBTs) are on the roadmap for cslib. Before I even think about diving into the notoriously heavy delete function or attempting to upstream anything, I’d love to get your feedback on my definitions and proof structure. I want to make sure my formatting and design choices align with your project's standards, and I am completely open to revising my work.

Here is my repo.

Any feedback, code reviews, or pointers would be highly appreciated!
